TASK: Audit design-token drift across the site. READ-ONLY. Do not modify any source file. Produce one report file.

It defines all design tokens as CSS custom properties: colors (--neutral-*, --chroma-*),
type scale (--text-*), font families (--font-*), tracking/leading, spacing (--space-*),
radius (--radius-*), and motion (--dur-*, --ease-*). Parse it first and hold the full token table.

Walk every page and component in the live app (routes: box, brain, creative, technology, about —

transition-duration, or easing — wherever it lives: CSS, inline JSX style props, hardcoded
hex/rgb/px/rem in JS/JSX, and hardcoded color values inside GLSL shader strings or Three.js
material definitions.

CLASSIFY each applied value into one of three buckets:
- EXACT       — uses var(--token) OR a literal that equals a token's value exactly.
- NEAR-MISS   — a literal that is CLOSE to a token but not equal. (Colors: within ~10 per RGB
                channel of a token. Sizes/spacing: numerically within ~15% of a token's value.)
                These are the dangerous ones — they look intentional but bypass the system.
- ORPHAN      — a hardcoded literal with no token cousin at all.
